subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: After an opt-in timeout releases a deferred-maintenance lane, should OpenClaw keep that session coalesced until the original plugin worker settles, or define a cancellable/replacement lifecycle that permits another maintenance run immediately?
rationale: The fence protects selected core side effects but cannot determine whether concurrent plugin-owned `maintain()` calls are valid; that is a durable lifecycle contract decision, not a mechanical test-only choice.

options.title: Keep coalescing until worker settlement
options.body: Keep the per-session maintenance ownership active after the queue timeout and allow only the already-running worker to settle before another deferred maintenance run is scheduled.

options.title: Define cancellable replacement semantics
options.body: Add a documented cancellation/ownership contract for context engines, then permit a timed-out worker to be replaced only after that contract fences all relevant plugin effects.

recommendation.title: Keep coalescing until worker settlement
recommendation.body: Keep the per-session maintenance ownership active after the queue timeout and allow only the already-running worker to settle before another deferred maintenance run is scheduled.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current timeout and fencing design and are the clearest available routing candidate for the lifecycle tradeoff.
